paper_metadata.title: Implementing Quantum Machine Learning in Credit Card Fraud Detection

summary: The paper proposes a hybrid variational quantum-classical fraud detection pipeline for a 284,807-record credit card dataset, using amplitude/angle encoding, a VQC, and a classical neural network on a Qiskit simulator. It reports recall 0.89, precision 0.82, F1-score 0.85, and AUC-ROC 0.91 on a 70:30 train-test split, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical baselines for the main experiment.

experiments.description: Hybrid variational quantum-classical credit card fraud detection using a variational quantum circuit (VQC) with classical neural network post-processing on a simulated quantum environment.

algorithm.variant: Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) hybrid with classical neural network

hyperparameters.dataset_features: 30 PCA-transformed features plus Time and Amount

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical transaction features are normalized and encoded into quantum states; amplitude encoding maps a feature vector into amplitudes, requiring approximately log2(N) qubits for N features. Angle encoding is also described as an alternative, mapping each feature to a rotation angle on a qubit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of credit card transactions as fraudulent or legitimate, minimizing classification error / weighted loss in an imbalanced dataset.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Weighted loss function to address class imbalance; threshold-based binary decision at 0.5.

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on a European credit card transaction dataset.

dataset_specification.description: September 2013 transactions; 284,807 records with 492 fraudulent (0.172%); 30 PCA-transformed features (V1-V30) plus Time and Amount; 70:30 train-test split.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Imputation of missing values, standardization of numerical features, categorical encoding, PCA-transformed features used; features normalized before quantum encoding.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single train/test evaluation on a 30% test split; metrics reported: precision, recall, F1-score, AUC-ROC.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Data cleaning, imputation, standardization, categorical encoding, PCA-based feature handling, normalization for quantum encoding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical neural network receives VQC measurement outputs and produces final binary classification.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical machine learning / classical neural network
speedup_claims.conditions: as quantum hardware advances; current experiment was run on a simulator
speedup_claims.caveats: No empirical speedup is reported. The paper only states that the hybrid approach could offer significant speedups in the future.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not established; the paper reports a simulator-based hybrid VQC + classical NN workflow with no runtime, qubit count, or scaling study.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline performance is reported for the main VQC+NN experiment
No hardware execution on a QPU

Hybrid model evaluated only on a simulator
Potential data-loading overhead for amplitude/angle encoding is not analyzed

notes: Paper explicitly states the experiment was conducted on a quantum simulator using Qiskit.
No explicit qubit count is reported; num_qubits is not specified in the paper, so it cannot be reliably extracted.
No asymptotic complexity or speedup order is characterized; speedup_order inferred as none_proven because the paper only claims potential future speedups and reports empirical metrics on a simulator.
The paper reports empirical fraud-detection metrics on a simulator: recall 0.89, precision 0.82, F1-score 0.85, and AUC-ROC 0.91.
It does not provide a direct classical-vs-quantum benchmark for the main experiment, so no demonstrated quantum advantage can be concluded.
